# Drawer — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a drawer when someone needs to pick, filter or confirm without losing their place: choosing a date, setting filters, confirming a payment method. It anchors to the bottom edge, so it works with one hand and does not fight the content above it. Keep the task to one decision — a drawer that grows into a form has outgrown itself and should become a route. It is not for navigation between places; that is the navigation drawer's job.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use modal sheets for tasks that need focus — the scrim marks the interruption.
- Let content scroll inside with titles pinned where applicable.

**Don't**

- Don't trap focus without announcing modality.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container | resting | comp.sheet.container | surface-container-low, 28px leading edge, level3 |
| Scrim | resting | sys.color.scrim | 32% |

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| DrawerRoot | Owns the open state. Accepts `open`/`onOpenChange` to control it. |
| DrawerTrigger | The element that opens the drawer. |
| DrawerContent | The panel. Portals to the end of the document, renders the backdrop and anchors to the bottom edge. |
| DrawerTitle | The accessible name of the drawer. |
| DrawerDescription | The body text, wired to `aria-describedby`. |
| DrawerClose | Closes the drawer from inside it. |

### FAQ

**Bottom drawer or side sheet?**

Bottom drawers rise for compact flows; side sheets dock for persistent panels.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a drawer when the content is secondary to what is on screen and should slide over it rather than replace it: filters, details, a short form. It is a modal panel with a title, and unlike most of this family it has a proper open STATE — `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` — so it works controlled or uncontrolled and reports every change. That is worth noticing, because `Dialog`, `Sheet` and `Snackbar` are controlled-only (`Dialog` and `Sheet` share the `open`/`onOpenChange` contract; `Snackbar` takes `visible` and `onDismiss`). If you are moving code between these surfaces, the missing uncontrolled case is the first thing you will hit.
